classifications.rationale: The President presently continues the Cuba national emergency, a self-executing legal-status consequence, while also assigning the Secretary discretionary rulemaking authority whose consequences would arise only upon later issuance; these materially different postures are combined in one sub-directive.
classifications.evidence: hereby continue the national emergency with regard to Cuba as set forth above and authorize and direct the Secretary of Homeland Security

classifications.rationale: The President authorizes, but does not require, the Secretary to issue vessel-anchorage and movement regulations; any regulated legal consequence occurs only if the Secretary later exercises that discretion.
classifications.evidence: The Secretary may make rules and regulations governing the anchorage and movement of any vessel

classifications.rationale: The President grants the Secretary discretionary operational authority to inspect vessels and place guards; the segment neither presently applies those measures to a vessel nor mandates a specified later outcome.
classifications.evidence: The Secretary is authorized, to the extent consistent with international law, to inspect any vessel

classifications.rationale: This segment inseparably aggregates discretionary enforcement authority and executive-branch assistance and delegation provisions with a hortatory appeal to nonfederal officials, supersession of prior proclamation provisions, and a congressional-transmittal command, which carry materially different postures.
classifications.evidence: I urge all State and local officials to cooperate with Federal authorities
